alignments.note: Conjunction γάρ rendered *For*.
Article to *the* under rule 19.
One Greek compound noun rendered *love of money*; head on *love*, which realizes the compound's semantic head φιλ-, with *of money* realizing ἀργυρ-.
Expressed copula.
Anarthrous predicate noun; the supplied *a* is its rule 7 helper under rule 51's anarthrous clause.
Genitive quantifier expanded with the generic noun *kinds*; rule 17 heads on the quantifier, and the case preposition *of* rides here because no article takes a determiner (rules 21, 23).
Article before κακῶν with no English determiner written; rule 23.
Substantival adjective rendered *of evil* (ASV margin: Greek evils); the case preposition stays with it under rule 21's determinerless clause.
Relative pronoun.
Indefinite pronoun.
Participle rendered by the phrasal *reaching after*, the particle being the English verb's own; headed on the verb word.

Aorist passive rendered *have been led astray*; the auxiliaries ride under rule 9 and rule 17's resultative clause heads on the meaning-bearing complement *astray*, which carries the πλαν- sense, *led* being the generic support verb. Heading on *led* remains defensible.
Preposition.
Article to *the*.
Noun.
Conjunction.
Compound verb rendered *have pierced … through*, the particle realizing the περι- prefix and the auxiliary riding under rule 9; discontinuous around *themselves* under rule 15.
Reflexive pronoun.
Adjective, split from its noun under rule 26.
Anarthrous dative; the case preposition *with* stays with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause, discontinuously under rule 15.

review_notes: πάντων takes the whole *of all kinds* with the case preposition, the article being `unrepresented` for want of an English determiner; giving *of* to κακῶν instead would leave the quantifier bare and is less natural to the ASV's phrasing.
The head of ἀπεπλανήθησαν is placed on *astray* under rule 17's resultative clause; *led* is the defensible alternative.
